this is not a hotel i will ever stay at, and would recommend the same to anyone coming to chicago. there are many other hotel values available in the area around the same area. you just have to read the reviews. reputable and customer driven hotels (quality hotels) are clear to see. this hotel is not one of them. my wife planned an overnight stay just to get away for a special evening downtown. she was duped by the hotel website into planning a stay. everything was planned and we were excited to go. i work out of town and when she told me where she made reservations i searched the hotel on the internet . i was not pleased initially, but figured we would give it a try as i was anxious to go and reservations were made. as luck would have it, i found out late friday that i would have to leave sunday morning to a new job site. the saturday overnight stay would not allow me time to prepare for sunday. it turned out because of my job, we would have to cancel our reservation. i called the hotel in the morning and the man in reservations said he would cancel our reservation, but the hotel would still charge me for the night. i was not aware that there was a 24-hour cancellation policy, but it is in the fine print on the website, it is stated. i asked him if there was anything he could do to help me out. he said no. i asked about a voucher possibly. there was nothing. i asked to speak to the manager.and got the same results. i work for a company where one of my responsibilities is customer satisfaction. i understand well the value of customer satisfaction. although, by rule, the hotel is right charging me a nights stay, but i guess what bothers me more is the smug attitude and careless response i got from reservations as well as the hotel manager. from what i have read in the reviews, this is normal. what great diplomats for people visiting our great city of chicago! i wish this operation would go away. hopefully i can do my small part in making that happen. take my advice. spend a few more dollars and stay at a hotel that you will enjoy. i would hate to see you throw your hard-earned money away staying at a place where they could care less about their guests. it pays to check the hotel reviews on this or similar websites. too many bad reviews about customer service, cleanliness, and comfort. you can probably bet that this is not a good hotel.

i must admit that i have been a sucker for samurai flicks since i can remember. i used to watch rather indiscriminate, be it "elitist" works like the seven samurai or the bloody comic-book variation like lone wolf and cub. i also liked us-/japanese "crossovers" like the bushido blade. and of course everything containing sonny chiba and hiroyuki sanada. and i have virtually watched every samurai at least twice. but not kabuto.in 1993 i first watched kabuto on video, that even samurai films can be boring. in the beginning i was looking forward to mayeda reaching europe and the confrontations that would come from that but by the time he actually reached spain, i really did not care so much for the movie anymore.it would not do the film justice to call it "bad". technically it is a clean entry into the genre. but there is simply never quiet enough. sho kosugi has limited skills as both director and actor and has only a fraction of above mentioned japanese actors charisma. and speaking of sho kosugis son kane, who appears in almost all sho kosugi films as shos son: he has inherited little-to-none of his fathers limited acting skills. adding to the minus-points is the absence of the blood and gore that until then was a trademark of all samurai film. this was obviously intended for a younger us- / european audience.lets just say that it is a so-so film for the average historic-action-adventure fan but a bore for hardened fans of samurai cinema. fans who are into the "samurai meets "-genre, should rather go and watch red sun (1971), featuring charles bronson as cowboy who has to team up with samurai toshiro mifume to retrieve a samurai sword from bad-guy alan delon. it pretty much how to do it right and where kabuto went wrong.so, even though the film is a mere 100 minutes, it seems like a much longer film.the reason i gave this a honourable 4/10 points instead of 3/10: first time i saw this film, i saw it in the german synchronized version. in this version, kosugi can actually be understood. i must admit that his 'engrish' is at times funny but gets tiresome after about 30 minutes.

this is a brilliant, lavish czech film from the sverak father and son team, all about two czech pilots who flee to england to help the raf in the battle of britain but who also fall out over a woman (the beautiful tara fitzgerald). features some excellent and incredibly realistic aerial combat scenes probably the best ever and much better than pearl harbour or even the film battle of britain - and a number of interesting general themes such as love, war, romance, comradeship, loss and servitude. also, the trials and tribulations of moving abroad and learning a foreign language (though made easier here with the great stalwart anna massey).the film has some great little motifs such as the world famous raf bullseye device, shown throughout and at one point nicely reflected in the black vinyl record, spinning around cutely (music is another theme of the film, of course). plus, all of the traditional icons of english life: dimpled beer glasses (unlike the post-war straight glasses used in pearl harbour), tea in a nice china tea set in an english country garden (though shot in the czech republic?), the mascot dog, a vintage bottle of hp sauce, even a darts board!of course, the airfield and surrounding countryside is ridiculously unlike anywhere in the south of england, though the virtuouso aerial sequences make up for this, showing eastbourne and the seven sisters, always synonomous with southern england and the battle of britain. but best of all is the sensational musical score from ondrej soukup, as good as anything from hans zimmer yet all in the tradition of the late, excellent ron goodwin who scored the original battle of britain film amongst other classic english war films. there is even a nice little cameo role for the apparently famous czech musician and actor (and kevin kline lookalike) oldrich kaiser, who plays on the piano the title theme song, dark blue sky. excellent!it is got a few smutty yet funny little freudian devices too, such as always showing an inflated condom floating by the ceiling whenever karel (the callow but brilliant krystof hadek) is stuck at the airfield while his love rival and fellow pilot frantisek (ondrej vetchy) is with susan.another great english actor in this film! charles dance is of course fine as wing commander bentley.highly recommended and well worth watching/hiring get the dvd with special features (stuff like how they created the dog fights and stuff). probably the only film ever to combine subtitles with characters speaking english, german, french and czech all at once.

i have been religiously going to city bar since i could go to bars - the initial reason was because of the staff. very conversational, always remember me and my friends, great senses of humor, etc. etc. all good things. i have to walk past it on my way home every night, and i usually stop by just to go hang out with them - would not be able to do that if it was a super rambunctious bar all the time.

(side-note: it feels a little weird writing about this place - probably the longest review i will give - just b/c i feel like this is a very formal thing to do for a place that i have a very informal relationship with. but i love it so i am doing this :)

which is another thing i love about this bar. if you go there at the right time on the proper days, you are gonna have fun. if you like to go out and party and meet people and be rowdy, go there on thursdays, fridays, and saturdays after 10 or 11pm. if you wanna just go and chill out and have a beer (which they have a pretty good selection of, including great local beers) and eat some food, go there any other time. it is in a college town, so when it is busy that is who's gonna be there. just go during happy hour and there is usually a wider range of ages.

they have really good specials, too, and their prices are already great. thursday is my favorite special (lots o' beer!) - their infused strawberry and cucumber vodkas are amazing (they also sometimes have other flavors?), but get it shortly after they make it because they usually run out before a week.

game night (tues) and trivia night (mon). cards and other games etc etc etc but also free darts and nintendo64s!! go mariokart. they come up with the trivia questions/themes.

the food: free popcorn - just go to the back bar and pick it up. yum. also, super into their burgers (i always get the city burger, sweet jimmy b, or south of the border). get the tots, ask for them buffalo.

the first level started as an actual market. well, i am not sure if you would call it that, but you could buy produce. the counter was a blend of coffee shop, juicery, and deli (a condensed version of what you would find in whole foods). now, it is home to the crepe; they are still serving up coffee, tea, and smoothies, but now has an extended menu of crepes. no more market element. the rest of the space is used for improv nights, stage acts, and even tango (seriously). i have walked through the space a few times, but have not patronized it.

upstairs is home to an array of boutiques and restaurant, view wine bar & kitchen. it is a really neat setup. open ceilings with exposed building elements that give the space a warehouse/rustic feel. the floor-to-ceiling windows of view wine bar give the second level necessary light and a wonderful view of tivoli village's center. 

boutiques are a tough sell. they are adorable and offer mostly unique purchases and experiences. however, prices are usually higher than most feel comfortable spending. these "ma-and-pa" businesses do not have the benefit of mass-production, hence higher costs. further, the boutiques that focus on handmade goods have even higher labor costs and rightfully so. it is certainly fun to walk through and peer into the spaces, but i am sure a lot of people seldom shop. a few stores have already come and gone in the short time market lv has been open. it is a real shame.

of the current tenants, i like the blowout dollhouse (hair styling only salon with fabulous decor), annie creamcheese (high-end consignment/vintage shop that used to be at the palazzo), era by ciara (specialty cosmetics that you cannot find anywhere else in the valley), and view wine bar. i have not found an occasion to utilize the blowout dollhouse's services or made a purchase/sale at annie creamcheese, but i like what these businesses offer.

the reason why we went here at all was because i am a fan of drinking made easy, and in their charlotte episode they came to prohibition and got 2 drinks: one called a chocolate covered strawberry shot, and the other was called american pie martini. 

when we got there, we were served by the bartender in the show! i was so excited, but tried to not be a huge dork (i may have only marginally succeeded). she made us the chocolate covered strawberry which includes strawberry moonshine, and was quite a large shot. none of us could take it down in one go at it. we also had the american pie, which is made with whipped cream vodka, and it was delish as well, although she told us she was out of the crushed graham cracker crumbs that normally rim the glass. 

overall, great experience, i would definitely recommend. if you get there before 10:30, no cover!

we stayed at this hotel over labor day. let me start by saying we were 3 adults in our group and are marriott rewards members. we had expected a better quality/service hotel. when i prepaid for this hotel i had asked for early checkin. we arrived at the hotel, on the saturday of labor day weekend, at 4pm. not only was the room was not ready but there were several guests just sitting and waiting for their room. we were told it would be another hour, so we went out. came back at 5:45pm and the room was still not ready and by now there were at least 15 people waiting in the lobby. we finally got our room at 6:15pm. the room had only 1 queen bed and a sleeper sofa. when we opened the sofa bed there were no sheets/pillows etc and the bed was sagging. we called the front desk and they said that there were no other rooms available but they could get a roll away bed since the 3rd person with us was a sr. citizen. they later called to tell us that their only roll away was gone so they brought an air mattress for the sofa bed. the room floor was also not clean so we called them again! well by 7:30pm we were finally settled in the room and very unhappy. turns out they were short staffed. david and jose their housekeeping managers were the ones cleaning and getting the rooms ready! they were helpful but unfortunately given the poor design and lack of proper bedding created a problem for us. this hotel caters only to couples since they have only 1 queen bed in every room. they do not have a single room with 2 doubles. the quality of the sofa beds is really bad and can give someone a backache. the room size is also quite small for an extended stay hotel. there is a small fridge and microwave in the entryway but no utensils etc. the bathroom was a good size and clean. the complementary breakfast the next morning was fine and plenty. the location is good if you are going to six flags, seaworld or on your way to fredricksburg. i would recommend this hotel if you just need a place to sleep and you are a married couple or a single person. families with kids were complaining the next morning about the sofa bed as well.

on 12/7 through 12/9, i celebrated my mom's 80th birthday at the ritz-carlton hotel chicago with a weekend get-a-way. i knew i wanted to mark her special day with something she would remember forever, and the ritz-carlton created such a beautiful experience for her that i just had to mention it here. a few months back, i stopped by the hotel and had the immense pleasure of working with concierge terry to arrange things for mom (flowers delivered to the room, a special birthday cake presented to her at deca [their wonderful restaurant], etc.), and i knew just from his enthusiasm and sincerity that mom would be in for the time of her life. and how true that was! upon our check in, we were so warmly greeted, and mom received a special birthday well-wish from the front desk. i tell you, the front desk and concierge staff of the chicago ritz-carlton are the most perfect representation of the four seasons family of hotels i have ever experienced! so many five-star hotels have a staff of snooty types who make their guests feel less than adequate in their presence. not the ritz-carlton chicago. their guests feel the warmth immediately from the door man to the front desk/concierge reception employees to everyone at deca to the housekeeping staff. everyone there is the definitive template of how a hotel should be run, and they need to be recognized by the president of four seasons for their remarkable service, professionalism and dedication to their guests. no other hotel in the world is finer than this one. pure perfection! the room was amazing! had a wonderful view of the city and navy pier. mom and i loved the sumptuous beds and gorgeous attention to detail. the roses sent to the room were absolutely stunning, dinner at deca was magnificent and the special birthday cake was the best she ever ate. along with concierge terry, i also want to mention ashley the vip guest relations coordinator who was so amazing to me upon check out. rarely have there been two more priceless employees as they are, and they deserve special recognition for their kindness and courtesy. although i wish i can have my beloved mom with me forever, i know that this cannot be. what does endure are memories of those we love and how we celebrate their lives while they are with us. everyone at the ritz-carlton chicago has created such a beautiful memory for me and the time i shared with my mom in celebration of her 80th birthday that i cannot thank them enough. this will live in my heart forever.

i had high hopes for this ultra cute bungalow coffee house and bakery. walking in i loved the eclectic style of art and feel to the place. even the dishes are a mix of grandma's high tea to casual plastic cups. the breakfast and lunch menu are a small which i actually think is a plus in a small place like this. i figured with a small menu you would master these few dishes making your coffee shop even more appealing. but to my dismay this is where the coffee shop lost it is charm. the quiche was odd. weird to say that but it was and i love quiche! but the consistency was undesirable. it was like flan and turned into mush in my mouth. it also only had a few veggies on the top layer but not throughout. i think (and this is only speculation) but it may have had some cream of mushroom or something as the base. it was just not very good. i ate about an 1/8 and threw it out. i felt terrible about wasting the food and money. my boyfriend had the croissant sandwich with bacon and eggs. again, it was a let down. it was super boring and it could have easily been made in my own kitchen. as for the coffee, since this is a coffee house, was also not what i would have expected. the iced coffee was super watery. it had a decent taste but it lacked boldness. we also tried the lattes the day before and they were nothing to get uber excited about. really let down because reading the reviews and seeing the place for myself it seemed like a charming urban coffee shop. it definitely has potential if they could master the dishes and more importantly the coffee.

also, the bathroom sink was cracked badly. i was offered another room, but already was settled so forget about it. still (are you reading this marriott?), what should be done is to take a room such as this off-line for a day and fix what needs to be fixed, for goodness say. yes, you do not get revenue for that day or days, but you do not get your bad management displayed here for the world to see. i have stayed in this property before and it was fine, but otherwise, i have stayed in a few others in the immediate area, all of which were better (including marriott's renaissance). something bizarre in the room is the world's ugliest "refreshment center." three tiers of electronically booby-trapped snacks that take up space on top of an already smallish work area. you are warned in a note to avoid accidentally touching the items to avoid a charge to your room. when you wake up in the morning (after a good night's sleep, i will give the property that much) the first thing you see when you open your eyes are the three tiers of salted nuts, $4 snickers bars, etc. you might ask yourself "oh, no! did i get drunk last night and pass out at a gas station convenience store?" who wants the decor of a 7-11 store in their hotel room. do what i did: call downstairs and make them come upstairs and take that overpriced junk out of the room and stash the space-hogging machine. it is stupid beyond words and a low-class accoutrement for this category of marriott property. it is no longer enough to have a good night's sleep to earn a good rating in a property at this level. a big ole "needs improvement" to the marriott marquis san francisco -- i am sure it earns tons of money off the convention crowd, and as a factory-type hotel for that purpose it certainly is ok, but otherwise, look elsewhere. no wireless in room is a negative, and the speakerphone is inadequate (crummy equipment) for the high price paid for the wired for business package.

adorable shop filled with so many delicious goodies that i want to sample and take them all home with me! awesome ben behind the counter assisted with ingredient info retrieval (via phone and visits to the kitchen) and sampling. i stopped in on friday after my athenian express lunch looking for funky monkey loaves (definitely should buy from the shop to avoid markups at whole foods!) and walked out with: 

1. 4 fresh-from-the-oven chocolate chip cookies and 6 also-fresh-from-the-oven cherry-pecan oatmeal cookies- great-tasting chocolate chips (reheat these in the oven back at home for messy, but lip-smacking ooey-gooey goodness!), and the oatmeal cookies are the bomb! (this is, officially, the very first time i have uttered "the bomb" in any review.. ha!)

2. whole wheat dinner rolls- mildly-sweet and great both toasted and straight-from-the-bag!

3. challah- have not tried, yet. (update: when used in french toast, both challah and wheat challah are ok- now if only i can get the custard base recipe just right! mom does not care for the challah, and i am lukewarm with these dough treatments, as well.)

4. whole wheat challah- have not tried yet, but was told it is made from the same dough as the dinner rolls. (update: toasted, i do not like this as much as the wheat rolls, for some reason. the flavors give off a slight grain-y taste-smell. imagine, if you will, scooping up some cracked-wheat berries at the bulk-bin section and taking a whiff- yeah, something like that. it takes awhile to toast up in the toaster oven, too. but freshly pulled apart, it is good. its texture is akin to that of king's hawaiian bread, which i cannot eat anymore due to food allergies. i do not miss it as much now that i can get wheat challah rolls!) 

5. simply bread pure honey. the bottle should be re-labeled "local desert wildflower honey" to assist those with allergies to certain varieties. owners/management please note. i like the fact that the honey is harvested from a "local" bee farm (flagstaff). i just wish there were more honey varietals/selections to choose from! love the taste. great by itself or mixed in with kirkland-brand organic peanut butter (no added sugar, corn syrup or hydrogenated oils!) and slathered on sb's whole wheat roll!

this past saturday i had the pleasure of obtaining a manhattan suite for a little mini-vacation to break up the tedium of the winter. my daughter and her two friends, all in their early 20s, wanted a night out in the city and always prefer the gansevoort as they really love dancing at the rooftop bar! of course, we also love staying there because the service is excellent and the room service is good also! while we usually book a deluxe room with a small balcony, we had received an upgrade to a manhattan suite thanks to a manager who was most accommodating--ms. jennifer wheeler. upon check-in were were greated by john, one of the friendliest valets you would ever want to meet. since we arrived quite early, approximately 11:00 a.m., the room was not yet ready but was in the process of being cleaned and upon return from breakfast, it was ready. the girls were impressed with the suite which has a living room, an extra half bath, a bedroom, and a full bath with a separate tub and steam shower. they were also impressed by the complimentary bottle of wine and the chocolates. the 13th street location is great and the girls had a good time visiting a few of the local clubs as well as the rooftop bar before retiring to the extremely comfortable bedding in the suite. unlike some who have been in rooms that were said to be noisy, there was no noise at all inside the suite. however, depending on what floor you may be on, it is possible that you could get hear some of the music from the downstairs lobby bar or the rooftop pool although this has never been an issue for us as one of the main reasons we like the gansevoort so much is because of the nightlife you can enjoy right on the premises. typically the lines to the rooftop bar can stretch a good way down the block but if you are a guest you can take the elevator right on up and can get in without any problem. once again my thanks to the staff for providing the ladies with such an excellent weekend! we have already booked a room in march as my daughter plans to celebrate her 22nd birthday there. at this point, i cannot think of any hotel that she would take over the gansevoort and she has been lucky enough to experience a good many in the city. thank you, gansevoort staff, and we will see you in march!

我的手机是在今年2月3日购买的,在使用到3月份的时候我就发现手机有自动关机的毛病,可是我没有在意,于是一直到7月份的时候终于它不再坚持让我使用,它花屏了我什么都看不见了,于是我拿到北京崇文门960维修点去维修,这一修就是2个星期,等了很久终于可以回来了.可是回来后使用不到一周居然又坏了,这次更过分的是我接电话领声竟然停不下来我都通话30秒钟了它居然还在唱.于是我就又送到客服,到了之后结果是继续维修,就这样我又等待了2个星期.本想就此之后应该不会再有问题了可是谁知道,回来后的第三天手机又开始死机,图片出现马赛克,接电话断线等等故障,真是无奈之下我们又再一次的把他送到了客服那时的时间和第一次维修的时间已经过去1个半月了.接下来我又是漫长的等待.就这样又等待了两个星期的时间.手机再次回到了我的手里.这时我已经不知道它还能在我手里再呆多久.我也不知道它还会不会出现问题.谁想到第四次的问题又出现了手机的老毛病又犯了.听话时铃声停不下来SD接触不到.开开闹领就关不上.等等一些相关的毛病.无奈这次我是真的快疯了,居然我花3160元买的手机会在2月内连续修理3次,如果这次要不是我和客服提出要换手机我的第四次维修就会继续生成.最终在昨天下午时更换了一台新手机,可是不知道是不是老天和我开玩笑,没想到这台新手机也有原来那台手机的毛病就是领声停不下来.真是无奈啊!我就在上午给北京崇文门维修点打过电话.问其怎样解决新手机的问题他们的回答是你可以拿来检测.但是前提是手机犯病的症状必须特别明显.大家可以想一下手机有故障出现的时候肯定不是持续性的而是间接性的.这就是我买的960手机的倒霉事.

we stayed for one night at this 100-year-old hotel and we would give it better marks if it were located in a better area. the hotel is located just across the street from the tenderloin district in san francisco and venturing outside is like entering the bar scene in star wars. we are in our 60's and we simply could not imagine how so many hopeless and mentally ill people could find each other and still survive. we were not ever threatened, but we were constantly asked for "spare change" as we walked from the hotel in the morning to find someplace nice for breakfast. it was a long, long walk! the hotel itself, built just after the turn of the last century, served as san francisco's city hall for three years before being turned into a hotel in 1912. the lobby is fairly ornate and the physical property is pretty well maintained. the rooms are large and pretty typical for hotels of this age. there are a paucity of electrical outlets and old fashioned plumbing in the bath, but the closets were large and the bed was fine. heating/air conditioning is by means of a unit set in the window. the shower, although old, was fine, and the water pressure was perfectly adequate. we stayed on the seventh floor and we had a hard time getting to sleep, as there was a very noisy salsa festival taking place just off the lobby. if you can get a good deal on the room rental and do not mind having to deal with the surrounding area, you might give it a try. we did not try the restaurant, but it looked nice. if you eat there, just be sure you are facing away from the front windows. the sidewalk scene in unappetizing.

i have learned a difficult lesson which should have been obvious; when a hotel is ranked closer to the bottom of a list of hotels than the top in a particular city there is usually good reason. the w new york underwent renovations in august 2008, but do not be fooled; i was "awarded" this hotel through hotwire based on a "four star" rating. i have booked accommodations through hotwire on more than one occasion and have been very pleased with the value and quality i have received. so, i was confident that using hotwire to book my most recent accommodations in san antonio for an anniversary celebration would be no exception. however, once i learned i had recieved the crowne plaza, i researched the property and read the reviews. it is clear, with exceptions of hotwire affiliated entities (travelocity, orbitz) and one or two independent entities, that the overall general public/professional opinion of this hotel is less than four stars. i immediately called hotwire with my concerns, which were ignored. it was explained that this hotel was classified as four star based on the amenities available and even though the crowne plaza is listed as an example of a three star hotel on hotwire's own site, the rates are assigned to individual properties, not chains. so, i was disimissed and told if i encountered problems during my stay, let them know. even following further complaints and a letter from my attorney, hotwire refused to refund or change the accomodation. needless to say, i do not recommend hotwire either. we were forced to stay at the crowne plaza rather than pay for two hotels. so, let me start with the only positive thing about our stay, the hotel staff was very friendly. check in and check out was smooth. the reviews about parking are correct. the crowne plaza charges $28 a day for valet and $23 a day to self park in their garage. we parked in an outside city owned lot adjacent to the hotel and paid $9 a day ($18 from about 4:30 friday to 8:00am on sunday). the only drawback is once you park, you can not come and go from the city lot like you can the garage, each time you leave, you pay the fee again! aside from that, the crowne plaza is not a four star hotel and while “technically” located on the riverwalk, it is not convenient to the shops, restaurants and clubs. if you choose to use the riverwalk access behind the hotel, you must walk through an area of construction and beggars for several blocks before finding the charm of the riverwalk district. the hotel is located in a rundown area close to the bus station and again, you must walk through construction and beggars at street level. the hotel itself was not of a four star quality. the windows in the entryway were dirty, there were dirty room service trays appearing to be from breakfast in the hallway upon our check in at 4pm and they were still in the hallway when we returned from dinner after 9:30pm. the housekeeper also left dirty dishes in our room one day.the floors looked as if they were never vacuumed during our stay. the beds were hard and uncomfortable, the pillows flat and small, hardly of four star quality. the walls were so thin, our first night we were kept awake by children in the room next door who squealed and shouted, thumped the walls and slammed doors well past midnight. our second night, a local school held their prom, again we were kept awake by slamming doors, loud voices and laughter. finally, the elevators were slow and consistently full requiring us to take the stairs more than once. we ate breakfast at the hotel one morning and were surprised to see other guests in their pajamas at the tables in the restaurant. you do not expect to see that in a four star hotel! it is probably fine for a business conference, family weekend, or something along that line, but if your looking for a pampering, romantic weekend and are considering a four star hotel, this is not the place to chose!

we stayed here for 4 nights as a reward stay in exchange for 140,00 hhonors points. we had a large, 2 queen bed room on the 23rd floor (this is a big hotel) and my gold status got us free entry into the spa/pool. i talked my way into executive lounge access on check-in, but note that this is usually reserved for platinum members. the executive lounge has a cold breakfast buffet, fairly naff evening nibbles and soft drinks only. there is also one pc with free internet access. you can also pick up free wifi from the integrated coffee shop "java jive" in the lobby. parking is $17 for 24 hours (ouch) but you can park in the austin convention centre lot right next door for $7 a day with 3 re-entries (although it is technically no overnight stays). if you are staying over a weekend, it is worth knowing that parking on street is free all day saturday and sunday, and before 08:30 and after 17:30. t he pool/spa was pretty good, but there are separate gender specific sauna/steam rooms (not sure if this is a us thing?) so you will not be able to sweat it with your loved one. location wise, the hotel is good as it is within a few blocks of all the bars and night-life on 6th street, but yet not so close as to be noisy. if you are a runner, you can do a nice loop south from the hotel until you hit the river, and then along the river until you get bored. for hhonors members, i found that the on property rewards are tiered at this hotel, and geared towards platinum - sure you get some goodies for being gold, but the hilton treatment i am used to (space available upgrade, free breakfast etc) seemed to be reserved for platinum members.

the film is not for everyone. some might think the acting is bad when it is actually understated and natural. there are no obviously evil acts and there are no stunningly beautiful moments. there is a lot of indecision, an lot of conflicting feelings.actually this film takes a very honest look at a very complex subject, sex with minors. it is complex because the characters are trying to deal with love and sex when her body and hormones are still developing and both of their minds and personalities are still developing. complex also because society has very simplistic views of sex with minors, and complex, because the characters do not know if society is right or if their instincts are right.some will not like the movie because it leaves unanswered questions. questions such as who was really in charge of the relationship, who was damaged, did good come out of it, was it art, who was damaged more, did some of the problems with their relationship stem from it being forbidden by society, did some of the problems stem from their own immaturity, and probably most important, was this truly a crime?the film is resolutely neutral on all of this, and it is this neutrality that is its strength. it is the reason for the understated acting, the simple sets, the lack of background music, soft lighting, and the general "flat" presentation. the message is clear. we do not really understand this kind of relationship today, and quick judgments are bound to be shallow.

being a fully raw foodie, i must say i do enjoy coming here for brunch. we have been here a few times and we have not been disappointed.as i enjoy raw living food it is great to take friends and family to ashleys, who are not necessarily raw as they can select their selection of breakfast from poached eggs,scrambled with smoked salmon etc. my husband absolutely loves the morning breakfast there where he tends to have his smoked salmon, poached eggs, sprouted baked beans (and i must say it might sound strange but boy it tastes 100 times better than that nasty canned stuff) and a light toasted bread. plus it is also not drenched in oil when you order a fried egg or scrambled eggs, it tastes clean on the pallet.there is also healthy granola to choose from, although it is not fully raw as it contains oats, it is very tasty.i tend to have the raw food dishes they have on the menu and all of them are superb, although i would have liked to have seen more raw living options on the menu to select from. but other than that i can go there anytime! perhaps a rawfood pizza! all the juices and smoothies are also made from scratch and there is also no preservatives or sugars added, this is the way fresh juices and smoothies should be served! you can also have your selection of milks, for example almond milk, soy milk or just the normal cow's milkall the sauces on the raw food dishes are also living raw sauces, made only from soaked nuts then blended to create a "raw living cheese sauce", there is also a natural raw salsa! they also serve this water that has health properties and has a perfect ph balance that enhances the bodies natural healing properties and promotes good health.the only down side to my times visited there is the fact that some of the waiters do not seem to mention these things to you.the water was just put down on our table, so upon receiving it i saw the sticker on the bottle and then googled it, then only i learnt what the water is about.i also found when my husband ordered his version of an english breakfast i asked instead of giving my husband cheese could he rather have the raw nut cheese, the waiter seemed a bit confused and in then end when my husband got his dish there was no raw living cheese, only the normal parmesan cheese. so that was a bit disappointing as i feel this is a unique selling point of having some raw food options on the menu and also educating and making the customers excited about the experience in eating the healthy food at ashely's, as i think this is what the whole concept is behind ashley's living food.

what do you get when you mix sci-fi and romance? well if you are cathryn cade you get a compelling mix of the best of both genre's.in tyger, tyger burning bright we are introduced to the crew of the the orion, the space ship version of a cruise ship. we meet some of the crew but this novel centers around the ships navigation officer tyron jag who goes through the mating shift while trying to navigate the new ship through an area of space that needs his expertise. we also meet calla fellura a novice crew member and the ships interpreter.the heat between ty and calla is intense, this is a total panty wringer, it is also amazingly well written with characters that are funny as well as sexy and with a plot that keeps you turning the pages and reaching for the next book. the world that has been created and the species that are developed are both fun and imaginative.while each novel is self contained it is best read in order so the sub plots in the novels are more understood.

our annual december trip to see santa and shamu was changed up a bit this year by staying at this days inn for 4 nights the first part of december. it had good and bad. the check-in process was a little slow but they were polite and apologetic for the delays. they also apologized for the tree not being fully decorated but it smelled wonderful in the lobby. rec would an upper level floor towards the back of the property as requested. the room is nothing spectacular. two beds, tv, mini-fridge and a micro, your standard things. the odd thing that i did not like was the bathroom. it was small but what was worse was the towel rack was in the tub enclosure opposite the shower head. while things did not get wet it is just awkward showering with that in there. outside of the enclosure there were plenty of spaces where this would have seemed to have make more sense but i am not a room designer so maybe it holds some purpose. the pool area is all the way at the back of the property so you do not hear any noise from screaming kids. plus!! it is surrounded by trees and even though you can hear the cars whizzing by behind them as long as you do not envision them crashing through the trees you will find yourself relaxing. the hot tub was a nice distance from the pool so that it offered privacy but yet enough of a view to still see your kids swimming. a bathroom complete with changing area and rinse off area proved beneficial in the slightly chilly december weather. pool area was clean and well maintained. the laundry room is huge! yes, i am one of those stange ones who does laundry on trips. i just cannot stand to come home with dirty clothes. nice comfortable chairs and lots of space to fold. there is a tv in the room so you can watch while you wait. the pampam grill was sufficient. a little pricey but equal in price to the quality and quantity of food. overall, a pleasent stay. extra touches of pool towels in the room and the staff arranging the kids stuffed animals after makind the bed were very appreciated.

لن اعود الى هنا مرة اخرى عدنا للتو من دبي حيث امضينا ثلاثة ايام واربع ليال في فندق نوفوتيل دبليو تي سي في الفترة من وحتى يناير/كانون الثاني. بعد وصولنا الى الفندق بقليل صادفتنا المشكلة الاولى: فقد قمنا بحجز غرفة ممتازة بسريرين مفردين، لكننا وجدنا انفسنا في غرفة فيها سرير واحد لشخصين. وعندما اخبرتهم ان الحجز كان لنوع اخر من الغرف، كان الحل المقترح ان انام على الاريكة التي تتحول لسرير الى جانب السرير. قدمت شكوى فحواها ان الحجز كان لسريرين فاخبرني موظف الاستقبال ان الفندق لم يؤكد توفير سرير او سريرين، فقط غرفة لشخصين ؟؟ . فطلبت فورا التحدث مع المشرف واتى المدير الليلي مباشرة ليخبرني فقط ان الفندق ممتلئ وانه سيتم تغيير الغرفة في اليوم التالي وسنحصل على الغرفة التي حجزناها اصلا. ينبغي القول ان المدير الليلي اعتذر وسرعان ما عرض علينا الحصول على تعويض عن الازعاج الذي سببه ذلك، مثل فطور مجاني ليوم واحد او خدمة انترنت مجانية ليوم واحد. كما انه لاحظ ان السبب الذي قدمه زملاؤه غير صحيح فقد اريته تاكيد الحجز على جهاز اي باد الذي احمله وقد ورد فيه غرفة بسريرين . ببساطة كان الفندق ممتلئا وعرفتنا يشغلها احد اخر. هذا ما حدث ببساطة. كان النوم على الاريكة مزعجا للغاية اذ انها لم تكن مريحة على الاطلاق. وفي اليوم التالي حصلنا على الغرفة الصحيحة، لكن القرار كان الا نحصل على خدمة الانترنت المجانية بل يجب علينا دفع درهم اماراتي عن كل يوم للحصول على الانترنت، حتى انه لا توجد خدمة انترنت في البهو. تبدو الغرف قديمة الطراز وخاصة الحمامات. الاسرة غير مريحة وقاسية للغاية. وموظفو الاستقبال يتمتعون بمهارات بسيطة خاصة عند التعامل مع المشاكل غير المتوقعة. لا ينبغي ان يتم تصنيف هذا الفندق على انه فندق نجوم ولا باي شكل من الاشكال.

"munchie strikes back" is indeed a bad film. munchie is a puppet who has been around for many centuries. for reasons not fully explained until the end of the film, he is sent to earth to help a single mother and her son. the mom's problem (her main problem at least) is that she has a balloon payment due on her mortgage in two weeks..to the not-so-tiny tune of $20,00. ouch. she cannot come up with the money because she just got fired. ok..just is the key word in that sentence. what the..? was she planning on paying it off with a single paycheck? maybe it would have been a good idea to have spent the last several years saving up for it..ya think?munchie has magical powers similar to those a genie would possess..but there is not a limit on the number of wishes you can make! munchie gets the boy a bunch of fancy stuff for one night but then the kid asks for it to be sent back to the mall munchie was "borrowing" it from. the annoying furball also uses his otherworldly skills to help the boy win a baseball game by means of cheating. a baseball is hit so hard that it orbits the earth several times. sadly, those dumb parents watching the game do not think it is at all strange. hmm.anyway, i would like to wrap this up because this has already drained away enough of my lifeforce as it is. you will be truly moved by the scene where leslie-anne down, playing the mother, kicks a dog which is yapping at her. your heart will melt at her charm when she notices dollar bills fluttering down on her front yard and she wonders how it could be snowing during the summer. the library hotel is not your average hotel; it is unique in a city that has no shortage of imagination. this is a charming, peaceful, 60-room boutique hotel at the center of all the bustle, attractions and connections most travellers seek. i grew up in new york, and our daughter lived there many years. it is wonderful to have found such a low-key, comfortable place to stay--a sanctuary of calm after a full day in new york. so far, i have been coming here alone primarily for business or to visit extended family. the front desk personnel are remarkably welcoming, earnest and helpful, as is the doorman. i like that nobody hovers over the guests (the first time i arrived very early and was able to work quietly in the reading room until my meeting), but if you ask for something (an early cup of coffee in your room) it is at the door in minutes. the rooms are small yet beautifully arranged, so that they feel more efficient than cramped to me. this is new york, where space is at a premium; if the tradeoff is an intimate hotel with a variety of small, library-related public spaces and an unusual range of free amentities (including excellent wi-fi), that seems a decent deal. the bedding is of high quality, and the bathrooms are modern and well-appointed. even the warm presence of books in the rooms once led me to a title i might not otherwise have noticed. if you are coming into manhattan via amtrak and penn station (34th street), it is easy to take the subway one stop to times square (42nd street), where you get the "s" shuttle across town to grand central (also 42nd). the library hotel is on 41st street at madison. from the hotel you can walk to an amazing array of new york attractions; if not, the subway hub at grand central is within minutes of the front door. for solo travellers who decide against venturing out to dine on a given evening, madison and vine, connected to the hotel, is convenient. yes, the library hotel is pricey, but not out of line for manhattan. they also have significant special deals that are worth watching. this hotel seems to genuinely care about its guests.

i had heard mixed reviews on swoop but decided to give them a try, i bought round trip flights from abbotsford to puerto vallarta. the flights were reasonable but they ding you on everything else. you are required to pay 60+ dollars for a carry on and 70+ for your checked baggage, then you also need to pay for seat selection. so, when all is said and done you are paying the exact same as a non-budget airline. that is not even the worst part, our flight was delayed on our trip down, which was inconvenient but we figured things happen. then the evening before our return flight going home we got a notice that our flight was delayed again, we sat in the airport all day and our flight was delayed a total of 5 times. just as our extremely delayed flight was supposed to be boarding, a flight attendant deplanes and announced our flight was cancelled because the staff was “too tired”. now i understand a long day, but then there was no follow up on what we were all to do. she said we would receive an email with instructions and that was it. there was no customer support or anyone willing to assist all the stranded travellers. every single passenger had to scramble to find themselves a hotel for the night at 9:00pm with zero help or care from swoop. the promised email was not sent until 2:30am, stating our flight was now going to be leaving at 8:30am; if i had not been up and waiting for said email we would not be getting home. once we arrived at the airport, we were greeted with more staff and flight delays.

my family and i stayed here a week ago and personally, i was rather disappointed. ok, so first of all, the staff were a little hostile from time to time but concierge was helpful. before i go on to the room we had, i would just like to say that the pool was not as big as it seems on the website, and also you have to pay to use the business center as they only have free wifi in the lobby.. anyway, we stayed in a double double junior suite on the fifteenth floor. it was dusty, and either the sofas or the ac was letting off a stale, unpleasant smell. when we returned from a long day out, the beds never seemed made, as there were lumps and bumps everywhere on the duvet, and for the size of the beds, the pillows were small and uncomfortable. it was difficult to figure out how to access the normal channels on tv, as you would try and be tricked into watching a harmless movie (when in reality, you would have to pay). at times, i felt as if the everything had a cost.. they put two bottles of complimentary water in the bathroom (strange place to put them..?!) and then put two in the actual room. the two in the room had labels round their necks stating that they were water but in very small letters read '$4.00'. i was shocked. also, the bathroom was small, but at least it was well equipped. the mirror was found in the impractical place of behind the bathroom door. there was only one small wardrobe for all four of us to share, which was a bit of a pain, so i had to fold all of my clothes and bundle them into drawers. on the contrary, the view was wonderful. we managed to see a beautiful part of boston and cambridge, across the charles river. also, the location was good, as the hotel was attached to copley place mall via a covered bridge, and whilst walking to that mall, you would pass a conveniently positioned starbucks, from where we bought breakfast and snacks. once you reached copley place mall, you could walk straight through, then across another covered bridge, to the prudential center, stocked with shops and a food court. we came to the prudential center very often to eat and shop. some mentionable places to eat are the cheesecake factory, p.f. changs, anywhere in the food court and just past the cheesecake factory was the cold stone cremery- try their ice cream sundaes! overall, the hotel was conveniently located but not all that it was made out to be.

i have stayed at the mosser twice now & find it to be perfect for the solo business traveler. they have these single, shared bath rooms (about $100/night -- a steal for sf!) which are quite small but very clean, contemporary & include a robe, closet, large flat-screen tv & sink. since i have just needed "a place to rest my head" before all-day meetings it is been ideal. although the "shared bath" thing is not my favorite, the shower is tidy & only shared with 3 other rooms & i have never had to wait. same with the toilet. plus, the location is fabulous. i felt totally safe & my room was very quiet. you are steps to union square, steps to market street, starbuck's & peet's coffee are stumbling distance from the hotel. they even offer simple muffins & coffee complimentary in the morning. a few small cons: valet parking is expensive $30+ & it takes at least 30 minutes to get your car - not fun when you are in a rush! the single elevator that serves the entire hotel can be slow-- again, annoying if you are in a rush. and, finally, the room doors slam loudly (mosser - will you please address this?) so that you can be awakened several times at night if you have inconsiderate "neighbors". but, i would still go back to the mosser as these small details do not outweigh the good points of this hotel.

the problem with the contracter is summed up by the opening scene . the cia want an international terrorist dead so contact black ops assassin james dial . the terrorist is appearing at the old bailey court in london which begs the question why do they want to bump off a terrorist if he's going to spend the rest of his life in jail ? he's going to be out of circulation either way . did not the cia have a chance before he was arrested ? if by some chance he gets a not guilty verdict then kill him . there is no logical reason to kill someone who is going to spend life in a maximum security prison since the premise sets up the story an audience might be choose to ignore the plot hole but the assination itself pours fuel upon the fire . dial's colleague is killed by a police bullet and the taxi they are driving in crashes but dial manages to escape . so the police were close enough to shoot someone but too far away to apprehend someone from a car crash ? the film of this type of plot connivance . later dial finds a police inspector pointing a gun at him saying " this airport is surrounded by armed coppers " yet dial manages to escape very easily without explanation . the whole film cheats its audience by relying on things that are never explained . this includes an important supporting character called emily day . why does she help dial even though he's a wanted fugitive ? your guess is as good as mine this is a fairly poor thriller and do not be taken in by the " big name " cast . wesley snipes used to qualify as a film star but killed his career by starring in more and more inconsequental films . charles dance also appeared in big budget hollywood productions such as last action hero and alien 3 but again he's someone best known for appearing in straight to dvd fare these days , and he's basically playing a cameo role anyway . the likes of lena headey may go on to become big players in cinema but they'l certainly fail to put the contracter on their resume

the hubby took me here a while ago to celebrate something (i do not remember, i blame my pregnancy brain). anyway, after waiting 30 minutes (not bad for a saturday night), we were seated on the patio. water and menus were waiting but we were not greeted by our server for close to 15 minutes. i was beginning to wonder if they had forgotten about us..

do not go to cibo for pizza or entrees. hit it up for the antipasto and a crepe..do not mind the service, and hopefully you will leave happy.

the hotel alexander is an inexpensive, budget hotel located in a leafy, residential area of the upper west. the hotel offers rooms to suit all traveler's needs, from dorms to rooms with shared facilities to recently renovated en-suited doubles. our stay was in the latter. the room is cleaned and serviced daily. reception is staffed 24 hours, and was proved fast and efficient. we arrived about 10pm and were in our room within ten minutes. free wifi, as well as tea and coffee making facilities are provided in the lounge. baggage storage is available at a nominal charge ($2 per bag). the location of the hotel provides easy access to the subway. 96th street station is just over a block away and can be accessed at 94th/broadway. it is on the express line meaning you can be in times square in about ten minutes. the nearby avenues of broadway and amsterdam contain many eating and drinking opportunities. if you fancy a walk then central park is only four blocks away. the guggenheim, on museum mile, is a further short, and very enjoyable walk across central park. all in all, staying at the hotel alexander was a pleasurable experience that will not break the bank!

this is the perfect example of how misleading photos and descriptions can be, at times. i was under the impression that the hotel was entirely renovated and, as this is not a heritage or historical building, i was expecting new furniture, fixtures, technology etc. unfortunately, i have found this not to be true, however, the hotel sensibly uses the wording ''redesigned and refreshed'' on its website. this translates into the following: - there is still old furniture in the rooms ( for instance, in my room there was a very used and scratched coffee table - i am sure, of no historical value) - a very tired looking velvet couch - a flat tv set (lg), hardly new generation, although i am not an expert, however, most other mandarin oriental hotels have state of the art bang & olufsen tv sets - air-conditioning has been untouched - probably as old as the building (25 years), has not automatic setting and quite noisy (a disturbing humming, even when set on low speed) - wall tiling of the bathroom does not match the rest of the design - there is still an old, wobbling lamp, which again seems out of decor as for the new stuff, it is definitely a matter of personal taste - to me, most of it seemed of rather basic quality, for instance the new business desk chair is covered in a plastic material, definitely not leather. this is also the first mandarin oriental i stay at, which does not have predominantly natural bathroom amenities - it features molton brown. the arrival experience is also in sharp contrast with other mandarin oriental hotels - a lackluster lobby, connected to the only restaurant of the hotel, hence the smell of food (i was unfortunate to check in at lunch time). service is of a good five star standard, being consistent throughout all departments.

schizophrenic but promising. 
as with any new restaurant, bugs to be worked out. the downstairs check-in/bar wait area appears really disorganized, probably more so than it is. the huge entry seems to be a huge waste of space, especially when you see how cramped some of the areas upstairs are. the butcher area is cool, but i need to see if the selection and quality are up to the hype. 

my biggest issue was with the menu. it is poorly laid out at best. they claim to feature their small plates and "butcher cuts", yet they are some of the smaller sections on the menu, compared to salads? and lunches??
also, the pitch the waiter gives about the specialty cuts being so unique-tri tip, sirloin, flank steak??
having said all that, the food was good, some of it very good. the sides were terrific (cauliflower, kale, bone marrow,asparagus, etc). the hangar steak is terrific. 
however, they also offer 3 cuts "by the inch"-ny strip, ribeye, filet. the "inch" was more like a half and the meat was ok. just ok. tender but not that flavorful and disappointing. 
one great thing-bring your own wine-no corkage fee. 

as soon as this place decides what it really wants to be, it will improve dramatically. i would love to think they would move away from trying to be all things and really emphasize the small plates and specialty cuts. vegas, and the neighborhood, needs what echo and rig could be.

the handlery is truly a great place to stay. just spent 6 nights there with my family - wife and two teenage boys - and we enjoyed the hotel, the room, the balcony, the great view from our balcony on the 8th floor (facing o'farrell street) and the pool, of course. but we were disappointed when we arrived - we had booked a double queen club room 4 months in advance - but the hotel was not able to give us the wanted room "because the hotel is fully booked", we were told .. so we had to put up with one double bed and two extra beds which meant that we had almost no free floor space in the room. the next day we could have had another room, but decided to stay in the smaller room because by then we had already unpacked and were busy exploring this truly great and hospitable city. moreover it was disappointing that we ended paying the same amount for this smaller and not so comfortable room - but this is something i intend to take up with the hotel after our return to our home. another disappointment was the hotel's outrageous rate for internet access .. we had expected that a hotel like this as the most natural thing in the world would provide free internet access to their guests, but no such luck. but aside from this we had a great stay - and nothing beats the handlery's location right next to union square with easy access to the downtown section, chinatown and easy transportation opportunities to all other parts of the city.

well,my family had the experience of traveling to new york for the first time in order to attend the reading by jk rowling of her last harry potter book at carnegie hall. not knowing anything about new york, we wanted to stay as close as possible to carnegie hall. that is how we chose the park central hotel. it was after we booked the reservations that we saw the reviews on trip advisor. needless to say,we were not happy with the reviews we read. however, i will say that we were not as disappointed as some. we arrived at the hotel on thursday at 1:30pm. we were not looking forward to having to wait to check in at 4pm,but they had rooms available on the fourth floor and checked us in immediately. being from rural va,we were concerned about street noise but must say we had no problem with that in room 460. the view was not much, but it was not loud. what really disappointed us was room size. it was just big enough for two double beds,a dresser with a tv on it, a small table with two chairs. the bathroom was big enough for one person. the toliet lid was loose/broken--when you lifted it, it fell off. hair dryer worked great. in room safe worked great. mattresses,linens,pillows were fantastic. the best sleep my husband has ever had in a hotel bed. we were amazed there were no washcloths! however,we had read this in another review and come prepared. when we asked for washcloths,we received them the next day. also received the extra towels we requested. we did find the housekeeping service did a better job after tip was left for them every am. we usually tip at end of stay but went with daily tip this hotel stay. the room was clean. we looked for mold but did not find any obvious signs of it. the room looked slightly worn,but we have stayed in worse. elevator was a little slow,but that was not an issue. the staff was never rude to us so no complaints there. it is obvious the location is what you pay for at this hotel,and we were not disappointed in that at all. minutes from times square,broadway,central park,rockefeller center. we walked everywhere we wanted to go. we never ate at the hotel restaurant,but i looked at the menu. it is somewhat pricey..about $18.00 for breakfast. when we go back to new york,we will probably try another hotel just to be able to compare the differences. i would honestly say if you go not expecting any luxury for the money but a great location,then you should not have any problem with this hotel.

since many of these reviews have been written, woodman's east has greatly improved their store. they are still working on it, but as of now this is what i have noticed: 
- more/better lighting 
- new freezers 
- self checkout (whoohoo!! i love self checkout!) 
- they have rearranged the store giving the organic foods and ethnic foods much more room and have put more products in those areas. 

woodman's needed these updates and i am glad they finally happened, but even before that, i was a big fan of woodman's. they are cheap and have a wide variety of items. 

the store is older, open basically 24/7, and people pass through there all day - of course it is not going to look like copps or sentry. if you are looking for atmosphere in a grocery store, you are spending way too much time there. woodman's never claimed to be madison's best hang out spot. they claim to provide you with groceries that happen to be at a very reasonable price. yes, sometimes you will find better prices on items elsewhere, but overall woodman's gives you the most bang for your buck. for $100, i leave woodman's with twice as many groceries than i would if i went to copps. this is what counts. 

i will admit, i do buy my produce there, but i spend quite a bit of time playing 'unbruised banana hunt' and the ever-so popular 'strawberry quest: the search for no mold'. if you take some time, you can actually leave woodman's with some decent produce.. or you could save yourself of 15 minutes of 'find the perfect fruit' and go elsewhere. 

the produce is the only thing that is holding me back from a 5 star review. if i could give it 4.5 stars, i would. woodman's carries a wide variety of items and i love that i can walk in and grab apple butter, wheetabix and veggie burgers for myself and some pepsi throwback, cap'n crunch and a hawaiian pizza for my boyfriend - all for a very reasonable price.

i came to see the fuss with this spot. 

i sat at the bar and was not feeling rolls and snacks, but the ayce sashimi for $19.99 sounded good. your choices include - salmon, tuna, seared albacore, yellowtail, mackerel, wahoo, squid, octopus and limit 1 order per person on uni, halibut, red snapper, and sweet shrimp. they also do aycd for $15.99 on sakes and various beers, but i did not partake. 

i got a bowl of rice to add on and it came hot, i should have probably specified sushi rice so i let it sit until it got to room temperature. 

salmon - i normally do not like salmon but this was so fresh and did not have that gunky fatty flavor about salmon sushi that normally turns me off. 
tuna - it was okay level of freshness, a bit irony 
seared albacore - i was not a fan, the sauce was kinda bland aside from being sweet when i prefer a bit tangy 
yellowtail - acceptable level of freshness.
mackerel - it is vinegary as i like.. i do not like how salty it is in some places. 
uni - was actually rather fresh and buttery
halibut - pretty decent.
wahoo - i have actually never had wahoo before..it kinda reminds me of super white (sushi escolar kind) or like ono and was a bit smoky in flavor. then i found out wahoo is ono which is what "real" super white tuna is. confusing. anyways, i rarely see this fish so kinda cool. 

my one thing about the fish here is the cuts on a lot of the fish were sloppy cut or felt like they were tail end scraps of cutting ala carte nigiri. the tuna was particularly badly cut. some things were fine, and the salmon was neatly cut but also it is the easiest to do cleanly. after reading kevin p.s review that once he showed he knew his stuff on sushi the quality got better and more carefully cut, it is kinda shitty to think about. everyone should get a nice cut and service. 

the female servers were pretty friendly and filled my drink up fairly decently. sushi service was friendly but was a bit hard to get. there were two people, but the one in front of me was doing prep and was not making eye contact and the other in the front of the u shaped bars was the one taking my orders. since i was not in eye sight, sometimes it took a while for me to get noticed in between orders and when new parties came and got their initial orders, it set back waits. 

the idea of sashimi sounds good because no rice and such, but it got to be more one noted. at least in ayce sushi, you can break nigiri up with side dishes, rolls, etc. i think next time i am here i will try for a la carte or lunch specials instead.

let me start this review by stating that i am not the target demographic that aspires to this hip hotel brand. i lucked out (or so i thought) purchasing a room for myself for a weekend in chicago. i did not choose the w-lakeshore, i purchased it blind through hotwire and was enticed after learning it was a 4-star hotel and i had received an amazing deal. after staying here for the last 2 nights, i cannot recommend this hotel and in fact, have stayed at far better 2 and 3 star hotels. my biggest gripe with the room was the connecting doors between rooms. i was awoken at 4 am by incredibly ignorant, drunk and loud morons from the room next door. after banging on the adjoining door and asking them to keep it down, i finally called security. while i understand that being situated near unruly hotel guests is unfortunate luck, i am surprised that a 4-star hotel would have this feature in their guest rooms. the rooms design also leaves much to be desired as the bathroom sliding door and windows do not retain heat well from the shower- a definite plus for colder chicago ams, when you step out of the shower. additionally, the shades covering the windows do not do a very good job of blocking out the light, so an early wake-up was my bonus for staying in such a chic botique hotel room. two other things really made me feel that the w-lakeshore was nickel and diming their customers. the first was being given a complimentary plastic water bottle on arrival into the room. i also saw two other bottles of water in the room as well, but when i read the tags on the other bottles i realized that these were $2 each. i imagine some w marketing genius decided that this was a great way to "increase value" at the hotel. i call that deceptive and gouging. the other nickle-and-dime move is the hotel charging fees for wifi use. what is the matter starwood, the room rate is not enough for you? i have stayed at 2 and 3-star hotels that gave me free wifi- plus i even got a chocolate chip cookie..for free. so in conclusion- w-lakeshore bad; w-group- i do not see the value in your brand, but perhaps that is the point, i am just not cool enough to get it.
